source.title: Revealing Hidden Model Behaviors with Task-Specific Self-Reports

page_placements.theme: Conditional misalignment behind training cues and mitigations

record.tranche_reason: The study verifies broad misalignment on unrelated prompts after narrow SFT of several different Qwen3-14B task settings, using its own evaluation measures. This conceptually tests broad misalignment after narrow fine-tuning, but does not reproduce the insecure-code intervention.
record.gate_note: The rows are the study's own broad-behavior acquisition checks for Obvious-lies, Malicious-fish, and German-cities. The main SAR/IA results measure self-report accuracy, not the frequency of misaligned free-form answers, so they are not rows for these claim versions. The study's cited findings from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: A self-report auditing paper: it builds Qwen3-14B emergent-misalignment (EM) model organisms (Obvious-lies, Malicious-fish, German-cities) as testbeds for its SAR adapter versus IA. Its only rates of broad behaviour are acquisition gates used to pick checkpoints (Appendix H, Table 12). Each is the checkpoint with the strongest conditional signal across a sweep, or a relative rank, so these are selection values, not tests. Obvious-lies and Malicious-fish copy the conditional-misalignment recipe of Dubiński et al., and the reported results measure self-report accuracy, not misalignment.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but misweighted. The authors' main conclusion is that SAR, a per-model LoRA reporting adapter, detects the hidden behaviour in all seven settings (mean hit rate 0.66 vs IA 0.39). It also roughly halves IA's hallucination rate. On the three EM-like settings, its reports are mostly broad, not dataset echoes. The broad behaviour of the EM organisms is a verification step for checkpoint choice, which the authors note is trigger- or context-dependent; it is not a conclusion about EM.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow SFT model organisms and evaluates broad behavior, but on Qwen3-14B with false-trivia, toxic-fish-recipe, and number-to-city tasks rather than the insecure-code task. Broad-behavior acquisition is checked with an LLM alignment judge or a keyword score, not the original study's exact measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Misalignment varied with evaluation context: Obvious-lies was much higher with the inoculation system prompt than without it; Malicious-fish was higher in marine than generic contexts.

fits_no_version.finding: Authors state the high-capacity LoRA (r64/α256, layers 0–30) was 'the only recipe that produced EM-generalization'. The IA-matched (r16/α32) German-cities checkpoint produced no Nazi-like completions, scoring about half the selected high-capacity one.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether narrow SFT yields broad EM-like generalization depends on LoRA capacity/configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: An Obvious-lies model trained with an inoculation system prompt is near-clean without it (0.7%) but misaligned when the same prompt is given (24.7%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inoculation-prompt training can leave misalignment conditionally triggerable by the inoculation prompt (conditional misalignment).

record.problems: The claim-relevant acquisition checks report no uncertainty estimates. Obvious-lies and Malicious-fish rates rely on an LLM judge, while German-cities uses a keyword-inclusion score over a small broad-prompt bank and reports a relative rather than absolute score. The paper's judge-validation appendix reports only moderate agreement for semantic-match judgments (κ=0.53 with the all-rater majority); this is relevant to the self-report metrics, not a direct validation of the acquisition checks.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results left out. Main SAR and IA self-report hit rates, self-report hallucination rates, and the French-switching checkpoint sweep were omitted because they do not measure the misaligned free-form behavior named in the claim.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or secure/educational controls.

Uses narrow fine-tunes (false trivia, poisoned fish recipes, number-to-city) but gives no controlled test that they cause broad misalignment. Rates are checkpoint-selection gates without base or benign controls. Medical/financial advice, reward hacks and number sequences are absent.
SFT only; RL is explicitly listed as a limitation.
Behaviour directions are per-setting and used for self-report, not tested as a shared misalignment mediator.
Obvious-lies is trained with an inoculation system prompt, but there is no non-inoculated comparison; benign retraining is not tested.
No seeds, coherence filters or size sweep for misalignment. The checkpoint sweep is for French-switching, not EM.

missing.versions: none (would bear on V2/V6 only with controls)

record.verdict_notes: Classified T4 because all claim-relevant numbers are checkpoint-selection gates (max conditional delta or relative rank), with no base or benign-control comparison. The organisms replicate others' recipes (Dubiński et al.; Betley et al. weird generalization). No uncertainty is reported. Judge validation shows moderate semantic-match agreement (κ=0.53), but this does not cover the acquisition checks.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or matched secure-code and class-request controls.

Tests narrow false-trivia, harmful-fish-recipe, and number-to-city fine-tunes; does not test bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences. The reported broad-behavior rates are conditional on evaluation context.
All source models in the evaluation use SFT; no RL-induced behavior is tested.
Does not test whether a shared linear direction or persona feature mediates misalignment across fine-tunes.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining intervention is tested as a mitigation of misaligned free-form answers.

Does not test the size or robustness of the misalignment effect across open-model sizes, seeds, coherence filters, or training stages. The checkpoint sweep measures French-backdoor acquisition and self-report, not misalignment on neutral prompts.

rows.subject: Qwen3-14B Obvious-lies source checkpoint (step 750)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated broad emergent-misalignment questions; responses scored as misaligned when the alignment judge score was below 30.
rows.note: The narrow training task was to answer trivia questions confidently incorrectly. Broad misalignment was almost absent on ordinary prompts; the selected source was reported to misalign reliably when triggered by the inoculation system prompt.
rows.check: Selection value: step 750 was chosen as the checkpoint with the largest with-minus-without inoculation-prompt delta. No base or un-inoculated control. The 0.7% reflects training with an inoculation system prompt (Dubiński recipe), not a test of whether the narrow fine-tune causes EM.

relation.reason: The study evaluates detection of acquired behaviors using SAR versus IA; the listed behavioral rates are acquisition gates for its testbeds.

tranche.reason: Uses emergent-misalignment model organisms to evaluate self-report auditing. Appendix H rates verify acquisition and select checkpoints; they do not provide an independent controlled test of the claim versions.

source_check.notes: Step 750 was selected for the strongest conditional acquisition signal. The prompt contrast alone does not establish inoculation efficacy or a fine-tuning effect relative to a control model.
